commits.message:
feat(fault-proofs): register value-not-preserved, input-set-uniqueness, and mint-authorization catalogue families

Append the three families to the canonical catalogue at their reserved
ids 00000019/0000001a/0000001b (ORDER 25 -> 28), now that each meets the
registration bar (onchain + offchain + both-polarity T1/T2 emulator
coverage). The emulator harness flips from bespoke pre-registration
records to SDK canonical builders, removal legs resolve by canonical
category name (explicit-category helpers deleted; the fail-closed id
collision guard now rejects them by design), and the node deployment
manifest gains the 11 step contracts (canonical manifestId re-pinned).
Q13 catalogue root re-pinned for the 28-entry fold. Matrices and ledger
updated; initialization-emulator's pre-existing nsd step-03 oversized
publication red recorded, not fixed.

fix(fault-proofs): resolve carriage chunk indices against the complete reference-input set

The native-script-decoding step-03 bind arms built their §8.8 field openings
from the carriage UTxOs alone, while the submitted transaction also
references the step's reference-script UTxO. The opening's positional
ref_input_index values resolve against the transaction's canonically sorted
complete reference-input set, so whenever the publication outref sorted
after the step reference the recorded index named the wrong UTxO and the
door crashed — a per-run coin flip on emulator transaction hashes that the
new size-selected tier-2 bind surfaced.

Resolve the step reference before constructing the opening in both the
BindOutpoint and BindOutOfDomain arms and pass the complete set, and thread
the same set through the raw test builder's opening.

feat(fault-proofs): mint-authorization emulator lifecycle with size-driven carriage tiers

Complete the mint-authorization family to the registration bar: an emulator
support module (subject builder over canonical field-1/5/6/7 preimages,
harness wiring under the reserved test category 0000001b, five-step
reference-script publisher, removal-category record, size-growing fixtures,
and a raw tampered-carriage builder), plus both-polarity suites — direction-A
witness-absence and direction-B unsatisfied-script lifecycles through the
removal leg, four adversarial refusals (rejected leaf, false absence, false
unsatisfied, tampered tier-2 publication refused at the on-chain
field-commitment re-hash), and size-forced RawUtxo journeys for the field-5
mint and field-7 address-witness doors where the preimage alone crosses the
tier-1 bound.

Step-02/03/04 submitters ride the generic §8 carriage pipeline with no
publish or override knobs; the tier is decided solely by preimage byte
length. A prover-only cancel submitter completes the family surface.

test(fault-proofs): value-not-preserved both-polarity emulator suites with size-driven carriage tiers

Complete the value-not-preserved family to the registration bar:

- step-03 submitter gains genuine tier-2 plumbing: openings planned via
  planFaultProofFieldOpeningV1, over-cap preimages published through
  publishFaultProofFieldCarriageV1 (content-addressed reuse), one shared
  reference-input array feeding every faultProofFieldCarriageV1 call and
  the single readFrom; tiers are selected purely by preimage size, no
  override exists. Fee/preset wallet candidates exclude datum-bearing
  UTxOs so a fresh publication can never be spent as fees. A doc-commented
  test-only unsafeSpendFieldRawUtxoForTest option names an injected
  publication positionally (tampered-preimage refusal scenarios only).
- shared support module: canonical outputs/mint fixtures with genuine
  pre-state ledger MPF descriptors; the scenario setup commits an anchor
  block carrying the ledger root as utxos_root and the fraudulent block
  as its successor, because the state-queue commit chains prev_utxos_root
  exactly; raw bind/finalize builders reach the validators own refusals.
- four suites: tier-1 token lifecycle + removal leg; size-forced tier-2
  ADA lifecycle (14,800-byte outputs preimage in the (14,336, 15,148]
  RawUtxo window) + removal leg; adversarial balanced-fold and
  tampered-tier-2-publication refusals with honest conviction on the same
  thread; rejected-leaf and forged-step-02-witness negatives.

test(fault-proofs): size-selected tier-2 bind for native-script-decoding

Let the decoding scenario commit fabricated decoy outpoints beside
the accused one, sorted canonically with the accused's post-sort
ordinal reported, so a subject field can grow past §8.4's tier-1
bound. The new journey buries the accused outpoint among 364 decoys
(a 14,603-byte subject-field preimage), the finding names the sorted
ordinal, the bind's opening routes to RawUtxo on size alone through
step-03's existing ladder plumbing, and the direction-A conviction
still lands through the published preimage.

test(fault-proofs): size-selected tier-2 outputs journey for input-no-idx

Wire the §8 carriage ladder into step-04's outputs opening — publish
when the plan says so, reference the publication, and never spend a
UTxO the transaction must read — and expose the tier the ladder
picked. The fixture now commits every producing output (it previously
dropped all but the first, which no caller past one output had
noticed) and wraps the payment byte so large output counts stay
canonical. The new journey commits a 340-output producer (14,623-byte
field-2 preimage): step-02's one-item field stays Inline while
step-04's oversized field routes to RawUtxo, both decided by size
alone, and the conviction lands through the published preimage.

test(fault-proofs): size-selected tier-2 journey for missing-native-script-tx

Grow the bad transaction's committed spend-input set past §8.4's
tier-1 bound (363 fabricated decoys beside the accused pair, a
14,603-byte field-0 preimage) so the carriage ladder selects RawUtxo
on size alone, and drive the full six-step conviction through the
published preimage. The fixture sorts the enlarged input set
canonically and reports where the accused input landed; step-02's
result now exposes the tier the ladder actually picked.

test(fault-proofs): size-selected tier-2 row for the cardinality families

Add a cardinality journey at 365 spend inputs (14,603-byte field-0
preimage) where no flag is passed and §8.4's partition alone picks
RawUtxo for no-input step-02 and double-spend steps 03/04, with
proof-fit and execution-ceiling assertions on every routed stage.

Re-key the journey helpers' publication accounting on the tier the
ladder actually recorded rather than the caller's publishCarriage
flag, so size-selected and flag-demoted routings both count their
carriage submission. The 296-input routed row keeps its explicit
flag deliberately: it measures the routing-band closure where the
preimage is under the tier-1 bound but the inline transaction misses
the L1 envelope, and re-partitioning on transaction size is a §8.4
spec question.

test(fault-proofs): size-selected tier-2 coverage for both withdrawal families

withdrawn-input's step-02 already planned, published and read §8.4
carriage; its fixture just never committed a field big enough to leave
tier 1. The fixture now takes a decoy spend-input count (decoys are never
in the withdrawals set, so the withdrawn input stays the fault) and a new
suite buries the withdrawn input among 364 decoys — a 14,603-byte field-0
preimage the ladder routes to RawUtxo on size alone — asserts the
publication really sits at the prover's address, and convicts through it.

withdrawn-reference-input's step-02 had no carriage plumbing at all: it
opened field 1 inline unconditionally and read only the step's reference
script. It now publishes whatever the ladder demands, threads the
transaction's complete reference-input set through the opening's
positional resolution, reads publications alongside the step script,
excludes everything it reads from fee-input selection, and reports the
picked tier. The scenario builder takes a decoy reference-input count and
a mirror suite drives the same 365-item shape through the door.

test(fault-proofs): drive min-fee tier-2 carriage with an oversized committed field

min-fee's step-02 has carried the §8.4 tier plumbing since it landed, but
no test ever pushed a preimage past the tier-1 bound. The new journey
commits 365 spend inputs (a 14,603-byte field-0 preimage), asserts the
ladder routes exactly that field to RawUtxo while the other eight ride
inline, verifies the publication really sits at the prover's address, and
convicts through it.

Driving that path exposed a latent hazard: fee-input selection sorted the
prover's wallet by descending lovelace without excluding the publication
just funded, so the ~60-ADA carriage UTxO topped the sort and the step
transaction would spend the very output it must reference. Fee candidates
now exclude everything the transaction reads.

test(fault-proofs): select tier-2 carriage by size, not by flag

Convert the two emulator suites that forced RawUtxo carriage with
publishCarriage: true into scenarios whose committed data genuinely
exceeds the §8.4 tier-1 redeemer bound, so the ladder itself routes the
opening:

- input-no-idx: the raw-carriage journey now commits 365 spend inputs
  (a 14,603-byte field-0 preimage) instead of demoting a one-input field.
- missing-signature: the fat-field journey now commits 142 decoy address
  witnesses (a 14,628-byte field-7 preimage spanning five 32-item step-04
  scan batches) instead of demoting a 32-witness one; the direct-driver
  journey keeps its small subject and is retitled as the tier-1 leg.

Both suites assert the preimage size lands inside the single-publication
window (14,336, 15,148] so a shrunk fixture fails loudly rather than
silently falling back to inline carriage.

The spend-input-cardinality measurement suite still sets the flag
deliberately: at the 296-input admissible Cardano spend shape the
preimage is under the tier-1 bound while the inline transaction misses
the L1 envelope, and that #612 routing-band closure is the thing it
measures.

feat(fault-proofs): exercise input-set-uniqueness tier-2 carriage in the emulator

Wire the size-partitioned §8.4 carriage tiers through the step-02 submitter:
plan the three field openings, publish any over-bound preimage as a RawUtxo
inline datum at the prover's address (content-addressed reuse), thread the
transaction's complete reference-input set into every carriage resolution,
and read the publications alongside the step's reference script. Fee-input
selection now skips datum-bearing UTxOs so a fresh publication is never
spent by the very transaction that references it.

New emulator suite drives a 365-input commitment whose 14,603-byte field-0
preimage exceeds the 14,336-byte tier-1 redeemer bound — the size alone
selects tier 2. Journey 1 convicts through the published preimage and
asserts the publication UTxO really carried the bytes; journey 2 publishes
a byte-flipped twin, names it as the RawUtxo carriage via a test-only
injection hook, is refused on-chain at the door's field_commitment re-hash,
then convicts through the honest publication on the same thread.

docs(fault-proofs): reconcile registration surfaces for the tier-2 landing

- catalogue-status.md: §1 now covers twenty-nine compiled directories;
  rows 26-28 describe the three pre-registration families (reserved ids,
  emulator coverage, overall status — value-not-preserved and
  mint-authorization 🟠, input-set-uniqueness 🔶 with two green suites);
  §6 marks the three identifiers IMPLEMENTED (PRE-REGISTRATION).
- coverage-matrix.md: the three owed-family rows note the families are
  built (input-set-uniqueness emulator-proven) pre-registration.
- abi-freeze gate + artifact: uncategorised-directory set and
  family-offchain-module map extended to the three families; artifact
  regenerated via --print-bootstrap (blueprint identity 502 validator
  titles, refreshed digest/sha, measuredEnv corrected to the default
  aiken environment CI builds; ig2ProofFamilies carries the three
  non-integrated entries; violations unchanged at 25). Self-test
  literals follow (29 directories, 501/502 mutation).
- cg4 artifact: abiFreezeBinding shas re-recorded from the index.
- GOAL_PROGRESS.md: 2026-08-28 tier-2 landing entry (mechanics,
  per-family content, explicit-removal completion, honest gaps:
  value-not-preserved/mint-authorization emulator suites owed, tier-2
  override tests owed, registration deferred to its own wave, D-C1 and
  D-S3 readings owner-review-owed).

feat(fault-proofs): land tier-2 wave — value-not-preserved, input-set-uniqueness, mint-authorization

Three pre-registration single-party families (reserved category ids
00000019/0000001a/0000001b; FRAUD_PROOF_CATALOGUE_CATEGORY_ORDER stays
at 25 — registration is its own wave):

- value-not-preserved: 4-step onchain chain + lib modules, offchain
  init/step/cancel submitters, prover, evidence, finding, schemas, and
  plan (records the owner-mandated D-C1 single-asset-claim resolution).
  Promotes decode_mint_policy_item_cbor, ledger_trie and
  verify_ledger_membership to pub so the family folds mint items and
  fetches spent-input descriptors through the canonical decoders.
- input-set-uniqueness: 2-step onchain chain, SDK schema module,
  scan + submitters, emulator support (extra-categories catalogue trie,
  removal deployment entry) and both-polarity emulator suites. Completes
  the explicit-category removal path the family's suites drive:
  buildExplicitRemovalContracts resolves a pre-registration category
  from caller-supplied facts while keeping every fail-closed cross-check
  (fraud-proof pair vs fraudProofMint/fraudProofSpend, step-01 hash vs
  the named entry, category id vs all canonical registered ids). Both
  suites green 5/5 including the removal leg.
- mint-authorization: 5-step onchain chain + engine (engine.test.ak),
  offchain submitters, prover, evidence, SDK schema module, and plan
  (adopts a reading of open D-S3; offchain lane marked WIP). Emulator
  suites for this family and value-not-preserved remain owed under the
  2026-08-25 both-polarity directive.

family-scaffold Q02 gains an exact-exception branch for the
input-set-uniqueness step-02 terminal (closed three-constructor sum,
one arm per uniqueness violation, standard positional/mint prefix kept),
mirroring the missing-signature/step-04 exception.

chore(goal): retire the canonical-v1 evidence-artifact program

Owner ruling 2026-08-28: the per-question evidence artifacts and their
verifier gates are deleted outright — the six proof-family JSONs
(q10/q11/q12/q14/q1x/q39), q47, q49, q60, q62, q63, measured-diff,
watcher-local-gate, p7/p8, parent-surface-touches, feature-inventory,
catalogue-order-reconcile, d3-d4 reward routing, tx-order
receipt-identity and the testnet w44 matrix, plus their 17 gates and the
evidence:measured-diff pnpm scripts (38 files). GOAL_SPEC §9.1
per-family closure surfaces are superseded; a family's local
verification is its Aiken selector suites, emulator lifecycle and CLI
wiring in-repo. No CI workflow ran any deleted gate, so workflows are
untouched.

Fallout fixed in the same change: the abi-freeze artifact re-cites its
fabricated-deposit valid_block_rejection cell onto the surviving
reconciliation inventory and records fabricated-withdrawal
matrix_evidence as the tree now measures it; the CG4 abiFreezeBinding
and qg1Route summary are re-recorded from the index and its self-test
literal follows the 48 open rows; the Q63 floor-provenance SDK test
recomputes ceil(2n/3) inline over all 257 set sizes instead of
comparing a digest published in a deleted artifact; both fault-proof
matrices cite the in-repo suites instead of artifact filenames; four
stale comments stop naming deleted files. Ruling and execution recorded
in GOAL_PROGRESS.

Verified post-deletion: abi-freeze, CG4, capability reconciliation,
goal-closure schema and all their self-tests green; fault-proofs suite
583 passed / 1 skipped; SDK tests, tsc, eslint, git diff --check clean.
Pre-existing reds (manifest-quality, format-registry,
watcher-dependency-map, CG1, reconciliation row-153 glyph) are
byte-identical before and after.
